# Incident Report: STRRAT RAT Infection — 2024-07-30

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 172.16.1.66 |
| MAC address | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F |
| Logged-in domain user | ccollier (domain WIRESHARKWORKSH / wiresharkworkshop.online) |

Confirmed by cross-referencing Kerberos AS-REQ CName (`ccollier`, `desktop-skbr25f$`), NBNS name registrations for `DESKTOP-SKBR25F`, and the malware's own self-reported beacon fields (below) — all three sources agree.

## Malware Family
**STRRAT** (Java-based RAT/credential stealer), **version 1.6**.

**Attribution basis: signature-confirmed.** The C2 traffic contains a plaintext, pipe-delimited beacon that is STRRAT's well-documented, hardcoded check-in string, sent every ~5 seconds over raw TCP (no TLS, no HTTP):

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender||1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>
```

Fields decode to: literal tag `STRRAT`, victim HWID `1BE8292C`, hostname, username, OS, architecture, installed AV (Windows Defender), STRRAT version `1.6`, country, and process uptime counter. This exact field layout is the documented STRRAT wire protocol, not a generic behavioral inference.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint (confirmed, signature match):**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` (TCP) — STRRAT C2 server. First contact at capture time 76.99s; heartbeat "ping" beacon repeats roughly every 5 seconds for the remainder of the capture (~508 seconds observed). Traffic is plaintext TCP, not TLS/HTTP — no domain name resolves to this IP in the capture (contacted by raw IP).
- Victim source port: 49754 (single persistent TCP session, stream index 83).
- Server never returns payload data in this capture — only TCP ACKs — so no inbound commands were captured, only outbound beaconing.

**Malicious/suspicious domains:** None resolved via DNS for the C2 IP itself (contacted directly by IP, a common STRRAT/RAT evasion trait). One other externally-facing lookup worth flagging as a secondary indicator (not malware C2, but consistent with the RAT's IP-geolocation/self-check behavior):
- `ip-api.com` → `208.95.112.1`, HTTP GET `/json/` at t=78.0s (~12 seconds after the GitHub/Maven downloads, ~1 second before the first STRRAT beacon) — returned geolocation for the host's public IP (US/Texas/Austin). This is a classic pre-C2 self-recon step seen in loader/RAT chains, occurring right at the infection pivot point.

**Likely delivery/staging (circumstantial, TLS-encrypted so file names/hashes are not recoverable from the capture):**
- `github.com` (140.82.113.3) then `objects.githubusercontent.com` (185.199.110.133/109.133/111.133/108.133) — 833 KB downloaded at t≈64.8–70.8s.
- `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209 / 199.232.192.209) — three large TLS sessions totaling ~8.9 MB at t≈68.0–73.8s.

These two downloads happen back-to-back, immediately followed by the `ip-api.com` geolocation check (t=78s) and the first STRRAT beacon (t=76.99s). The size and timing pattern (small GitHub object + large Maven download, consistent with a JAR loader plus a bundled/portable Java runtime) is consistent with STRRAT's known Java-based delivery chain, but because both sessions are TLS-encrypted, no file name or SHA256 hash could be extracted from this capture. Flagging as **circumstantial staging indicators only** — not confirmed as the drop mechanism.

**No file transfers with recoverable names/hashes:** No cleartext HTTP file downloads, SMB file writes, or exported objects containing an executable/JAR payload were found in the capture (`tshark --export-objects` on HTTP yielded only benign objects: a Microsoft NCSI connectivity-test text file and the ip-api.com JSON response). All payload-bearing sessions in this capture are TLS-encrypted, so no transferred file names or SHA256 hashes can be stated as evidenced by this pcap.

## Summary
DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as domain user `ccollier`, is compromised with **STRRAT v1.6**. Confirmed via the malware's own signature beacon string over its C2 channel at **141.98.10.79:12132**, active continuously from t=77s through the end of the capture. A GitHub + Maven download sequence and an ip-api.com geolocation check immediately precede first C2 contact and are the probable (but not hash-confirmed) staging/delivery artifacts. No evidence of secondary payloads, lateral movement, or data exfiltration beyond the beacon channel was found in this capture window.
